# Sugarcane ratoon management — gap filling and rotation
## When to preserve the ratoon
A ratoon with a stand gap of 20% or less should be kept. Manage trash as mulch,
shave stubble to encourage uniform sprouting, and fill only the very poor gaps.
## When to selectively gap-fill
Between a 20% and a 40% gap, fill only the missing stools and keep the field.
Monitor tiller count and maintain soil moi

# Sugarcane red-rot management — field hygiene and resistant varieties
## Choose resistant planting material
Use varieties rated resistant to red rot for the coming season and source seed
cane only from disease-free nurseries. Avoid planting seed from a field with
visible symptoms.
## Field hygiene
Cut the crop at ground level and remove infected stubble after harvest. Do not
leave infected trash

# Sugarcane heavy-rain advisory — Sohna block
## When an IMD heavy-rain warning is active
Suspend irrigation immediately and clear the furrow outlets so standing water can
drain before the soil waterlogs. On heavy-clay (drainage class C) fields, also
avoid field traffic while the soil is saturated.
## Action priority
| Priority | Action | Drainage note |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Suspend irrigation | Al

# Sugarcane water productivity under deficit irrigation
## Study setting
A two-season field study on loam soil at Sohna compared a deficit irrigation
schedule against a fixed calendar. The objective was to hold yield while cutting
the applied water.
## Finding
Scheduling on the depletion threshold rather than a fixed interval used less
water at a small yield cost in the water-limited season. Yield
